items.title: ‘My main goal is to help people’: I’m single, 74, with $10 million burning a hole in my pocket. What should I do?
items.description: “I also own my home and an SUV outright, with no outstanding debt.”

items.title: My mother, 91, has dementia. Every bank says I need her signature to unlock her $100,000 stock certificate. What can I do?
items.description: “These shares are the only assets in her estate without designated beneficiaries.”

items.title: Does a 2% beneficiary inherit 100% if the 98% beneficiary dies in a car accident? Asking for a friend.
items.description: “I’m curious what would happen if the account owner were to die suddenly at the same time as the 98% beneficiary.”

items.title: Microsoft’s stock seals its longest winning streak of the year as AI software fears fade
items.description: Microsoft’s software offers capabilities that will be critical for AI, one analyst notes.

items.title: ‘We are committed Christians’: Our son and daughter-in-law cut us off over politics. Should we change our $3 million will?
items.description: “We are hurt and confused, but we have also tried to respect the boundaries they have established.”

items.title: Nvidia’s revenue forecast is so huge that Wall Street wonders if SpaceX is the reason
items.description: SpaceX plans to spend tons of money on chips and recently announced it will only buy Nvidia’s. But other high-profile companies need more processing power as well.

items.title: My contractor handed my $42,000 pool upgrade to a subcontractor I had already rejected. What can I do?
items.description: “I specifically rejected Contractor A because of his reputation.”

items.title: Dolly Parton’s music, books and theme park see spikes in interest following her death
items.description: Dolly Parton, musician, actor and literacy advocate, died on Tuesday at the age of 80.

items.title: Kevin Warsh gets what every Fed chair hopes for: a bond market that trusts his word
items.description: Kevin Warsh passed another big test as a new Federal Reserve chairman on Friday: He said the central bank still has work to do on inflation, and the bond market took him at his word.

items.title: AI wants to help you pick a Medicare plan. Should you let it?
items.description: Using artificial-intelligence tools to help navigate Medicare’s open-enrollment season might seem like an easy way to simplify what can be an overwhelming decision.
